title: The k-th Smallest in a Search Tree
statement:
A binary search tree has `n` nodes numbered `1..n`; node `1` is the root. Node `i` holds a value `v_i` (all values are different), and you are given its left and right child (`0` means none). For every node, all values in its left subtree are smaller and all values in its right subtree are larger.

Find the `k`-th smallest value in the tree (counting from 1).

## Input
The first line contains `n` and `k`. The next `n` lines give `v_i`, the left child and the right child of node `i`.

## Output
Print the `k`-th smallest value.

## Constraints
- `1 <= k <= n <= 8000`
- `1 <= v_i <= 10^9`
- The input is a valid binary search tree rooted at node `1`.
